scope: Proposition 2.4 (Association and conditional order) of the manuscript “Gaussian free-field limits of weighted integer Lipschitz heights” (preprints/Gaussian-free-field-limits-of-weighted-integer-Lipschitz-heights-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 232 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3dae0156982e5d20), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 9. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every feasible history, the unobserved (B, τ) variables are positively associated. Two laws with ordered histories and common E0 are stochastically ordered, including the unequal extreme pins just described. Extra prescribed open-plus cells only in the upper law, or open-minus cells only in the lower law, can be incorporated by observing those cells and all their first-spin sites also in the other law. These claims hold for clipped cells and at x = 1.
